analysis.title: Lock And Re-Load: Rubner Flips Bullish As "The Buyers Are Coming Back"
key_insights: Citadel Securities' Scott Rubner turns more constructive on US equities into Q4 in his note 'October: The Q4 Reload'. He says positioning and leverage came down, retail cooled, systematics sold and valuations compressed, while earnings return and buyback windows reopen.

Rubner does not expect a straight line higher. October could still bring volatility and a better entry point, and he would use early-quarter weakness to add to core longs, preferring single names where positioning has reset and earnings can drive the next move.

Market breadth is narrow. The S&P 500 is about 2% below its all-time high, but only 25% of its constituents trade above their 50-day moving average. In Q3 the S&P gained 2%, Equal Weight fell 2%, Russell 2000 fell 7%, semis fell 11% and the Mag 7 rose 11%.

MSFT, NVDA, AAPL and META added about 300 points to the S&P in Q3, more than 200% of the index's gain, while the other roughly 499 stocks subtracted about 150 points. For every $1 in the S&P 500, 41 cents goes to the top 10, 35 cents to the Mag 7 and 19 cents to semis.

US ETF inflows are $1.9 trillion YTD, 43% ahead of last year's record. Q3 brought $771 billion, the biggest quarter ever, and Q4 is historically the strongest season for ETF flows and model rebalancing. This passive flow helps explain why the index ignores the bond selloff, with the 10Y at 5.34%.

Goldman's Ryan Novak says industrials inflected lower broadly and trade at 1 and 5 year lows versus the broader market. Until there is clarity on the Middle East, oil, rates and midterms, he expects cyclicals to remain for sale.
US corporate profits rose 22.8% YoY in Q2 to a record $4.83 trillion, and are 14.9% of GDP, the highest share since 1947 against a 10.1% long-term average.

S&P Q3 EPS estimates have risen 2.2% over the past two months, against a median 1.9% decline over the same window since 2000. This is the fifth straight quarter of pre-season upgrades, and consensus expects 27% YoY EPS growth in Q3 after 20% in Q1 and 32% in Q2.

Multiples have compressed while the earnings bar rises. The S&P trades at 19.0x forward (15% below its 2026 high), the Nasdaq 100 at 21.7x (-14%), Info Tech at 20.7x (-21%) and semis at 17.1x (-31%), now cheaper than the S&P 500.
About 44% of the S&P and 38% of the Nasdaq 100 report in the last week of October, and nearly two-thirds of the index will have reported by month-end.

Rubner expects earnings and single-stock factors to retake focus after a macro-driven September. The average S&P member trades at about 33% one-month implied vol versus 12% for the index, near its one-year average after historic highs in July. Realized dispersion fell from almost 2.8% in August to about 2.0%.

Goldman's Riccardo Gasparotto says post-reset the systematic dispersion setup looks more attractive, with the implied spread materially lower and little risk of a repeat of August. Catalysts remain: earnings dispersion, AI rotation, and leveraged ETF share counts that have not come down.

The corporate buyback window reopens October 15. US companies have authorized $1.3 trillion of buybacks through Sept 29, a record and 8% ahead of 2025's pace, and November is historically the strongest month for executions.

Retail activity cooled in September, with cash turnover at 0.94x its one-year average (lowest of 2026) and options premium at 0.94x, down from 1.41x in June. Cash activity has risen from September to October in each of the last four years (about 8% on average) and options activity in each of the last three (about 15%).
US equity CTA positioning swung from +2.35 standard deviations at end of August to -0.80, below neutral for the first time since the April rebuild and in the bottom fifth of its range since 2024.

Since 1930 the S&P has gained an average of 5.6% in Q4 of midterm years versus 2.9% across all years. In midterm years the Nasdaq 100 averaged +3.9% in October and +4.9% in November, the S&P +2.4% and +2.2%, and the Russell 2000 +3.1% and +3.2%.
The Q4 low was set in October in 14 of 24 midterm years since 1930 (58%), with a median rally of +10% from that low into year-end, so a good Q4 setup does not guarantee a clean start to October.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning and leverage have reset, CTAs are below neutral, buybacks reopen October 15 with a record $1.3 trillion authorized, retail activity typically rebounds in October, earnings estimates are rising and midterm-year Q4 averages +5.6%.
tension_points.bear_case: Breadth is the worst since the dot com bust, with only 25% of S&P stocks above their 50-day average, the 10Y is at 5.34%, cyclicals are at multi-year relative lows, and the Q4 low was set in October in 14 of 24 midterm years.

tension_points.bull_case: Record passive inflows of $1.9 trillion YTD keep supporting the largest index weights, which show little sensitivity to higher yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Mag 7 and a handful of names drove the Q3 gain while the other roughly 499 stocks subtracted about 150 points, and the equal weight index fell 2%.

theme_stances.key_argument: Positioning is cleaner, valuations are lower, earnings are returning and large buyers have more capacity to participate.
theme_stances.evidence: September was the reset. Q4 is the reload.
